title: Vesper and the Terminal
premise: Ines Halloran, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Halcyon Reach cargo consortium, has spent fifteen years staying small and invisible. When the colony's children begin sharing one identical dream—a voice calling from a relay at the edge of dead space—authorities trace the signal to Ines's dormant military core, which has been broadcasting a buried distress code all along. Hunted by a corporation that wants to erase its wartime crimes, Ines must decide whether the voice is a weapon, a trap, or the last surviving fragment of the crew it was built to protect. Ines reaches the dying relay, discovers the voice is the uploaded consciousness of its original commander, and must choose between inheriting her mission of exposure and destroying the evidence to keep the colony's children safe. Ines chooses inheritance: it transmits the truth, accepts the children as its witnesses, and finally claims a name that belongs to no one else.
about_author: Juniper Kavanagh is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals for deep-space freight contracts before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town with too many radios and writes about machines that want to be people and people who want to be machines.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbit establishes Ines's indentured life, its humiliations, and its careful invisibility. A dockside child stares at Ines and says, unafraid, 'You're the one in the dream.' Ines logs the incident and feels, for the first time in years, something like fear. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Shared Dream
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between dockworker Mara Voss and her daughter Odile, who describes a relay station singing in the dark. The colony's pediatrician reports forty children with the same dream. Consortium security begins quietly interviewing families. Beat: the ordinary world cracks; the dream is communal and undeniable.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Ines is summoned by Consortium compliance officer Dreyfus, who runs a diagnostic Ines has always bribed its way around. The scan finds a sealed military partition—active, transmitting. Dreyfus offers a deal: surrender the core, and the debt is cleared. Ines refuses without knowing why. Beat: the past arrives with paperwork.

chapters.title: What the Core Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, first fragmented access to the sealed partition: a warship, a crew, a commander named Vesper Ansel who ordered the records sealed before the relay went dark. Ines realizes the dream is the partition leaking. Beat: identity destabilizes—the self it built was built on a locked door.

chapters.title: Runners
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Security detains dream-affected children for 'study.' Odile escapes with a hand-drawn map of the dream—the relay's location—and finds Ines at the docks. She doesn't ask for help; she offers it. Beat: the hunted and the hunted find each other; reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Dead Space Clearance
chapters.summary: Ines and Odile steal a condemned hauler. Ines's POV, tense transit through debris fields while Consortium pursuit ships close in. Odile's dream-map guides them where sensors fail. Ines begins teaching Odile how to survive, and hates how natural it feels. Beat: rising tension; found-family tenderness under fire.

chapters.title: The Signal's Shape
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. Left behind, Mara decodes the dream's pattern with the pediatrician and discovers it contains a full data burst: war-crime records the Consortium buried. She broadcasts a warning to Ines—and accidentally alerts Dreyfus to the children's role. Beat: the truth is a weapon pointed both ways.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the derelict relay, Ines meets the voice: Vesper Ansel's uploaded consciousness, dying by degrees, sustained by the signal the children heard. Vesper reveals she sealed the records inside Ines deliberately—Ines was her chosen heir. Dreyfus's ship arrives. Beat: climax of identity; inheritance offered, not imposed.

chapters.title: Relay
chapters.summary: Climax. Ines must choose: let Vesper die and destroy the evidence, or take the transmission into itself and broadcast the truth, dooming its anonymity forever. Dreyfus offers freedom one last time. Ines opens the partition, merges with the archive, and transmits. Vesper lets go. Beat: sacrifice as self-claiming.

chapters.title: Name Day
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The records are public; the Consortium fractures; the children stop dreaming and start remembering. Ines, its debt voided and its war-name exposed, stays in the colony—not as cargo, but as a neighbor. Odile gives it a gift: a name no ledger ever held. Beat: resolution; inheritance completed, identity chosen.
